title: Checks for 0.0 / 0.0.
summary: It’s less readable than f32::NAN or f64::NAN. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Warns if an integral constant literal starts with 0.
summary: In some languages (including the infamous C language and most of its family), this marks an octal constant. In Rust however, this is a decimal constant. This could be confusing for both the writer and a reader of the constant. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Catch casts from 0 to some pointer type
summary: This generally means null and is better expressed as {std, core}::ptr::{null, null_mut}. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for array or vec initializations which contain an expression with side effects, but which have a repeat count of zero.
summary: Such an initialization, despite having a repeat length of 0, will still call the inner function. This may not be obvious and as such there may be unintended side effects in code. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for maps with zero-sized value types anywhere in the code.
summary: Since there is only a single value for a zero-sized type, a map containing zero sized values is effectively a set. Using a set in that case improves readability and communicates intent more clearly. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.
